"The chance of human extinction is about a coin flip, in my view," Geoffrey Irving, a former OpenAI and Google DeepMind employee, said in a new interview. title: (No AI) OpenAI launches Dots, its Muse competitor
author: Emma Roth
content:
![An illustration showing Dot avatars](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Dots-Hero-Image.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Like Muse, OpenAI’s Dots are represented by cute, customizable avatars. | Image: OpenAI

OpenAI is responding to Meta's [buzzy Muse AI](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/999526/meta-muse-ai-agent-hands-on-shopping) with agentic helpers of its own: Dots. During its DevDay keynote on Tuesday, OpenAI announced that Dots will serve as always-on AI assistants that can "do nearly anything" across connected apps in the background while learning your preferences over time.

The company's [capable GPT-6 Astra model](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/989601/openai-gpt-6-astra-release) powers Dots, which use their own cloud computer to access a web browser and more than 4,000 supported apps. You can interact with a Dot through a text-message-like interface that's [similar to the one offered by Muse](https://www.theverge.com/tech/993391/meta-muse-ai-hands-on), as well as hop on a voice call with it from ChatGPT on the web, desktop, or mobile.
